summary: Training over the last 4 weeks has been highly inconsistent, with only 9 sessions logged against a structured plan, no pool swimming at all, and chronic sleep deprivation (multiple nights under 5 hours, including a 41-minute night on Jul 27). Recovery metrics are concerning with body battery frequently in the 20s-30s range, and the Jul 18 run at avg HR 179 bpm signals a significant overreach event. Cycling volume is minimal relative to Ironman demands, and there is a complete absence of structured running sessions aligned to the marathon pace target of 5:45/km.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep as a non-negotiable training input — multiple nights of 3-4 hours are actively eroding adaptation; target a minimum of 7 hours before any moderate or hard session.
Begin pool swimming sessions immediately: zero pool swims have been logged in 4 weeks despite Ironman swim targets of 1:50/100m — start with 2x per week at 1,500-2,000m and build from there.
Introduce at least one weekly run at marathon target pace (5:45/km) for 20-30 minutes within a longer easy run to build pace familiarity, given the marathon is only 192 days away.

Cap running intensity: the HR-179 effort on Jul 18 at 5:02/km pace is far above aerobic threshold and counter-productive for base building — restrict all runs to below 160 bpm until sleep and body battery are consistently recovered.

Treat the upcoming Week 6 long ride (84km) with caution given the very low body battery on Jul 30 (max 2); if body battery is still below 30 on Aug 1 morning, reduce to 50-60km at Z2 only rather than risk further fatigue accumulation.
